hypothesis: Does the trained native admission/join system preserve simultaneous true relations with a shared subject, retaining old two- and three-hop answers after a new fact and interruption, or does exact functional-map memory overwrite an old branch despite available slots?
prior: W-NCI03 achieved bounded positive on four five/six-edge graph motifs, but stored all relationships as one outgoing value per subject. General-purpose relationships often require multivalued subjects; this remained untested.
frozen_method: Exactly the previously frozen 6-parameter learned join and 65-parameter native admission, 16-slot exact native recall with experimental 7-entry cap. Three motifs with same five pre-update edges and one later edge: root fork, internal fork, no-fork control; all queried by the same learned predicate and exact symbolic two-hop oracle. Seeds 23744..23767, 24 per motif. Frozen original edge ordering creates branch facts before querying. No model tuning.
outcome_criteria: FUNCTIONAL_MAP_FORK_RETENTION_FAILURE when no-fork original two-hop >=85% but BOTH root and internal forks each <50%; MULTIVALUED_TRANSFER_DEMONSTRATED when control and both forks >=85%; else MULTIVALUED_MEMORY_LIMITATION_NOT_ISOLATED. Always report oracle, retention, interruption, new fourhop, direct-only and resource counters. Do not declare native learned relational storage or full NCI01 on any result.
controls: No need to rerun NCI03 original
Store exactly <=7 active relation sources in candidate; exact multiset oracle max six edges, not learned and not compute comparable
Only dev training qualification before first sealed use, original artifact then rubric
Full Go regression and independent archive-only verification
No FORGE, CKB/KTRADE, accepted refs or production
